Delegate inside your organisation

{{ c.warn }}

Delegate to your urbanXtracts rep

NOT A DECIDED CAPABILITY
The mechanism is designed and the button is here so it can be reviewed, but it does not function and should not until three people have answered one question. A rep approving your order means the seller is approving the buyer’s purchase commitment — a segregation-of-duties and contracting question before it is a feature: who is committed, on what authority, and what your written authorisation actually says.

Open with sales leadership, the CCO and Legal. It also needs a standing written authorisation held on your account — a document under Documents, not a click on this screen.

What a delegate can never do

A delegate approves an order. A delegate does not lift a block, and no delegation can be configured to.

License gate
A location whose licence has lapsed cannot be ordered for, whoever holds approval.
Account ordering hold
An explicit portal store status may block submission at order entry. A QuickBooks balance is visible context and never changes that hold automatically.
Available quantity
An order above what exists is not approvable into existence.

The clock

How long an approval may sit
Reviewable baseline. Owning department first, then Executive Member for blocked or high-risk overdue work. Store expansion remains held, but the clock must be explicit before this becomes a live retailer workflow.
What an order will show
Whoever holds authority and until when, named on the order itself and kept there permanently. An order approved under a delegation says so on its face for the rest of its life.
When authority is withdrawn
It takes effect at once. An approval already in flight still names the person who held it — the record does not rewrite itself.

Reads, limits and the log

Every read is logged
A read writes the same audit event an export writes — scope, row count and the field list. You can read your own entries under Your records, which is also where a revocation lands.
Scoped to your licences
A credential reaches the licences it was issued for and no others. Narrowing a credential to one location is the normal case, not the exception.
Rate limit and page size

Revocation is immediate
Revoking stops reads at once rather than at the end of a session, and the credential cannot be un-revoked \u2014 issue a new one.

How financial visibility affects ordering

Separate controls
A non-zero or past-due QuickBooks balance is displayed here but never creates an order hold by itself. The portal’s explicit store ordering status remains the only receivables-related gate.
Buyer scope
Buyers see invoices and payments only for stores assigned to their profile. A store without a direct QuickBooks customer mapping stays blank instead of falling back to an organisation-wide customer and leaking another store.
Payments
Payment collection stays outside UX OS through the approved cannabis-banking process. The portal displays the latest QuickBooks payment history but never accepts card or bank details and never creates a payment transaction.
Source
Every live figure comes from the last fully successful server-side QuickBooks snapshot. A failed refresh leaves the prior complete snapshot visible with a stale warning.

Request access

For a new store, or an existing one adding and changing people. Everything here is a request: we qualify each licence against the state record ourselves, and terms are set before an account can order.

Banking, remittance and signatory details are not asked for here and should not be sent. They are collected once, in the onboarding record, and never live in the portal.

WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND IS NOT IN THE EXPORT
Cost, margin, discount depth, ownership code and rate cards do not appear on this screen and are not in the file it produces — the export is the same authorization rendered a second way, never a second authorization. Recall and lot impact

Lineage runs forward from an inbound lot to one allocation. This runs the other way and answers the only question a recall asks: who has this. Internal only — and it is not the escalation path. A product-safety issue goes to the CCO immediately and is itself a recall trigger; this is what the escalation uses once the CCO has decided.

THE WORDING IS NOT OURS TO WRITE
The portal carries whatever wording the CCO has approved and never composes it. Acknowledgement is recorded against the account, never against a named person — the store decides who answers for it. A store sees the notice on the affected order and on the lot, and nothing else: no internal owner, no clock, no lineage, and never another account’s row.

Documents

The paper between us, in one place — what you send and what we issue. The license gate has told a blocked shop to upload its renewal since the first draft of this design, and until now there was nowhere to upload it.

AN UPLOAD NEVER LIFTS A GATE
Sending a license renewal does not clear your license gate. The gate reads the license record, and an urbanXtracts reviewer updates that record after looking at the document — otherwise a file attachment would clear a compliance block. Banking, remittance and signatory details are refused here and stay in the onboarding record.

Measurement

The build plan says amazing is a buyer reordering in under thirty seconds without calling a rep. That is a measurable claim, so it is measured. These figures are live from your own use of this prototype — walk the catalog, trip a gate, look a tag up on the kiosk, and they move.

{{ measureSession }}

{{ r.q }}
{{ r.counted }}
{{ r.value }}
{{ r.why }}
WHAT IS NEVER COUNTED
Nothing ties a budtender lookup to a consumer. The kiosk has no person behind it and gains none here: a lookup is counted per device and per day, and the thing looked up is never joined to who was standing there. There is no identifier for a shopper anywhere in this, and adding one later would be a decision with its own sign-off rather than a schema change.
WHAT THIS PROTOTYPE CANNOT SEE
One session is one observation. A median and a ninetieth percentile need a population, and the interesting half of the gate question — what a blocked user did in the next ten minutes — needs a real deployment and a real telephone log. What is proven here is that the events exist and can be counted at the moment they happen, which is the part that cannot be added afterwards.

Kiosk modes

Configure the product experience for shared retailer devices. Every mode uses the Canix-backed catalog, hides price and internal account data, and keeps product copy factual for budtenders.

KIOSK MODE
Shared retailer product-education device

READY
Budtenders can inspect identity, format, product profile, package tags, lab state, cannabinoid values, terpenes and the original COA when Canix supplies them. Effects, medical claims, internal cost, exact inventory totals and retailer accounting data are never part of kiosk mode.
